What AgentOS does: the key is stored encrypted with the Android Keystore, injected only at the moment a model request is sent, and never written to logs, diagnostics or notifications; the agent\'s code doesn\'t run as root, so models and plugins can\'t reach root.

We recommend the acp-bridge that ships with the project (tools/acp-bridge in the repo): connect your computer to the phone over USB, tap “Generate pairing code” below, and run acp-bridge pair <pairing code> on the computer to pair for the first time; after that, set acp-bridge as the Agent command of your ACP client (such as Zed). If you only run adb forward tcp:8765 localabstract:agentos-acp, an ordinary ACP client won\'t send the pairing handshake and can\'t connect. Confirmations on the phone still appear as usual; the computer can\'t bypass them.
Lets a computer connect over adb. Turning it off disconnects it and voids all paired computers.

Not configured: when a caller has several past sessions, a new session is created every time

When the user (or another app) doesn\'t specify a session, AgentOS sends the current question and summaries of that caller\'s own few most recent sessions to the Jev service, which picks the session to continue; if it can\'t pick one, a new session is created. It works without this setting, with a new session created every time. The summaries contain the question-and-answer text of the sessions, not the model key.
